zh.question: 没有肌肉的植物，也能很快合拢、慢慢弯曲吗？
zh.observe: 依次试三站：含羞草局部轻触和主叶枕响应；捕蝇草一次、连续两次和隔久两次；幼苗左侧光、右侧光和两侧光。换观察视角不重置实验；换条件则开始新实验。比较哪一种改变膨压，哪一种快速改变叶片形状，哪一种依靠生长。

academic.title: 同一株植物，运动器官有层级
academic.body: 小叶、羽片和叶柄基部都有叶枕，不能把它们当成同一个关节。轻触可让信号沿所触羽片传播，小叶依次向上合拢；较广的响应还可能到达主叶枕，使叶柄下垂。放大纵切专门表示主叶枕，所以局部轻触时它保持原状。植物利用膜电位与钙信号协调响应，没有神经元或神经系统；电信号相似并不意味着存在动物式神经传导。

academic.title: 碰一次，为什么还不夹？
academic.body: 研究观察到触发毛受刺激后，钙信号传播并逐渐回落；短时间内再刺激，可能达到闭合条件。快速阶段涉及叶片曲率变化与弹性失稳，不能把它画成含羞草叶枕的简单复制。 本例用约 30 秒的信号整合窗口比较结果，不是所有植株都遵守的硬阈值；一次缓慢弯毛也可能产生多个信号。柱高和曲线是定性示意，闭合被放慢；没有模拟消化、实际捕食和数小时以上的再打开。重新实验是回放，不是瞬间生物恢复。

academic.title: 它是在转身，还是在长？
academic.body: 以幼茎向光性为例，蓝光感受及生长素运输、响应的不对称参与调节两侧细胞伸长。背光侧伸长较多，整段幼茎逐渐弯向光源。根对生长素和环境的反应不同，不能照搬本图。

zh.misconception: 没有肌肉，不等于不能动；几种植物也不是同一套动作。捕蝇草的短时信号不等于人的思考；幼苗向光弯曲不是被光拉过去。
zh.boundary: 三个独立教学实验没有共同的真实时间轴。含羞草的恢复被压缩，捕蝇草的闭合被放慢，幼苗以延时显示。模型是定性示意：不是显微照片、实测钙浓度或生长预测。捕蝇草的约 30 秒窗口不是普遍硬阈值，一次缓慢弯毛也可能引出多个信号。重放和重新实验不代表真实植物瞬间恢复；不要反复刺激真实植物。

narration.label: 植物也会动
narration.text: 植物没有我们的肌肉，也不会提起花盆走路。可是有些叶子会很快合起来，有些嫩茎会在生长中慢慢弯曲。今天看三种动作，先猜什么会让它动，再看看它靠什么做到。
narration.cue: 依次指出三站，停在含羞草展开状态。

narration.label: 含羞草改变支撑
narration.text: 先在画面里轻碰含羞草。细细的羽片上，小叶子不是一下子全合上。触碰引起信号，叶枕里的离子和水重新分配，膨压改变，叶子就能改变姿态。再看看主叶枕和同一个运动细胞，分清小叶的合拢与叶柄的下垂。等一等，它还能慢慢恢复。
narration.cue: 局部轻触，再比较主叶枕响应和运动细胞。

narration.label: 捕蝇草等待更多信号
narration.text: 再看捕蝇草。红色叶面上有细小的触发毛。这个实验中，短促地碰一次，叶子还张着；很快再碰一次，信号能叠起来，捕虫叶才迅速夹合。隔得很久再碰呢？先前信号已经回落。这不是它在心里数数；叶片和信号有自己的变化过程。
narration.cue: 比较一次、连续两次和间隔四十秒两次；查看动作来源。

narration.label: 把生长快进
narration.text: 最后看一株幼苗。光从左边来，它会慢慢向左弯；光从右边来，新一轮实验就向右弯。背光一侧的细胞伸长更多，整段嫩茎便渐渐弯曲。旁边两侧受光的幼苗也长高了，只是没有向一边弯。植物的动作，有些要等时间过去才看得清。
narration.cue: 左光与右光分别做新实验；放大生长区，对比两侧光的幼苗。

en.question: Can plants without muscles close quickly and bend slowly?
en.observe: Try three stations: local mimosa touch and the primary pulvinus; one, two close and two spaced flytrap touches; then left, right and two-sided light for a seedling. Changing view retains progress; changing conditions starts a new trial. Compare turgor change, rapid leaf deformation and differential growth.

academic.title: Different organs move at different levels
academic.body: Pulvini occur at leaflet, pinna and petiole bases. Local touch can trigger sequential upward leaflet folding along the touched pinna; a wider response may also reach the primary pulvinus and lower the petiole. This longitudinal section specifically shows the primary pulvinus, so it stays still during the local-touch example. Plants coordinate responses through membrane voltage and calcium signals, but have neither neurons nor a nervous system. Electrical signalling does not imply animal nerve transmission.

academic.title: Why does one touch usually not close it?
academic.body: Experiments show a calcium signal spreading and then declining after a trigger hair is stimulated. A further stimulus soon afterwards can reach the closure condition. The rapid phase involves curvature change and elastic instability; it is not a copy of a mimosa pulvinus. This example uses an approximately 30-second integration window, not a universal hard threshold. One slow hair deflection may itself produce multiple signals. Signal bars and curves are qualitative, closure is slowed down, and digestion, actual prey capture and reopening over hours or longer are omitted. New trial is replay, not instant biological recovery.

academic.title: Is it turning, or growing?
academic.body: In shoot phototropism, blue-light sensing and asymmetric auxin transport and response help regulate cell elongation. Greater elongation on the shaded side gradually bends the shoot toward the light. Roots respond differently to auxin and environmental conditions; this picture does not describe every organ.

en.misconception: No muscles does not mean no movement, and the plants do not all use the same mechanism. Short-lived flytrap signals are not human thinking; light does not pull a growing shoot.
en.boundary: These independent teaching experiments have no shared real-time clock. Mimosa recovery is compressed, flytrap closure slowed down and seedling growth shown in time-lapse. Geometry, calcium signals and growth are qualitative, not micrographs or measurements. The approximately 30-second flytrap window is not universal; one slow hair deflection may produce multiple signals. Replay and reset are not instant biological recovery. Avoid repeatedly stimulating real plants.

narration.label: Plants move too
narration.text: Plants have no muscles like ours and do not pick up their pots and walk. Yet some leaves close quickly, while young shoots slowly bend as they grow. Explore three movements: first predict what will trigger each one, then look at how the plant does it.
narration.cue: Point out the three stations and begin with open mimosa leaves.

narration.label: Mimosa changes support
narration.text: Touch the mimosa in the picture. Its leaflets do not all close at the same instant. The touch produces signals; ions and water redistribute in the pulvini, changing turgor and posture. Explore the main pulvinus and the same motor cell, separating tiny leaflet folding from petiole drooping. Given time, the plant can recover.
narration.cue: Try local touch, then the primary pulvinus and motor cell.

narration.label: The flytrap awaits more signals
narration.text: Find the fine trigger hairs inside the Venus flytrap. In this experiment one brief touch leaves it open. Another soon afterwards lets the signals build up and the leaf snap shut. Wait a long time instead, and the first signal has faded. This is not counting in a human mind; signals and leaf tissues have their own physical processes.
narration.cue: Compare one touch, two close touches and a forty-second interval; inspect the mechanism.

narration.label: Fast-forward growth
narration.text: Now watch a seedling. Light from the left makes the shoot gradually bend left. A new trial with right-side light bends it right. Cells on the shaded side elongate more, curving the growing shoot. The seedling lit from both sides also gets taller, without bending sideways in our comparison. Some plant movements become clear only when time passes.
narration.cue: Run separate left- and right-light trials; enlarge the growth region and compare the two-sided control.
